To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
SPECT MPS has prognostic value in patients with suspected and known CAD and in those following MI.
SPECT MPS provides prognostically important information in patients with known or suspected CAD and following MI, and that this information may be used to guide management.
SPECT myocardial scintigraphy provides independent prognostic information in patients with suspected and known coronary artery disease.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development, evaluation and use of new and improved diagnostic and prognostic tests and strategies for patients with suspected or established coronary artery disease (or following myocardial infraction) and the development and evaluation of new treatments for such patients.
the use of single photon emission computed tomograph (SPECT) imaging of the heart to assess the extent of damage to the heart muscle.
the prognostic performance of SPECT MPS in patients with suspected and known CAD and those following MI.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
SPECT MPS is useful in the risk stratification of patients with suspected or proven coronary heart disease.
SPECT MPS has a role in the risk-stratification of patients with suspected or proven CAD and in patients following MI.
SPECT MPS provides important prognostic information that helps to guide the management of patients with suspected or confirmed CAD or following MI.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

SPECT MPS provides important independent information to that from exercise tolerance tests and/or coronary angiograms that helps to risk stratify patients with suspected and known CAD and those following a myocardial infarct, enabling them to managed more appropriately.

SPECT is a very useful tool to evaluate the risk of coronary disease in patients with suspected coronary disease, or following myocardial injury, as well as to assess the risk of future cardiac events.

SPECT MPS is a valuable tool in assessing prognosis in patients with suspected CAD and following myocardial revascularization, and may help to identify patients at low risk for whom invasive angiography may be avoided.
The main takeaway from our work is that
SPECT myocardial scintigraphy provides important information about myocardial perfusion and function, and this information is prognostically relevant.
SPECT MPS has a prognostic value that is independent from that provided by clinical history, ECG, ETT and coronary angiography.
SPECT myocardial scintigraphy is an important prognostic tool in the management of patients with suspected or confirmed coronary artery disease.
